newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 17.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- WATCHDOGS LINK TO AVOID 'ANOTHER BARINGS'

A report by Britain's Securities & Investments Board and America's Commodity Futures Trading Commission, outlining measures aimed at preventing a repeat of the Barings collapse were sent to international regulators yesterday. The report follows a meeting of regulators from 16 countries last May in Windsor. The report recommends that regulators in different countries swap information on large positions built up by firms, increase the transparency of markets, enhance measures to protect clients' assets and adopt market crisis procedures.
-- RAIL GROUP CONSIDERS MERGER OPTION

Angel Trains Contracts confirmed yesterday that it is carrying out a review and considering its options, including a merger with another operator. The train leasing company privatised in January for 692 million pounds stg is carrying out a review due to the new competition in the industry as a result of the merger between Stagecoach and Porterbrook. National Express, the bus and coach operator, who were interested in Porterbrook, are thought to be a prime candidate for any kind of deal with Angel.
-- REFUGE-UNITED TIE PUT BACK ON HOLD

The proposed merger between life assurers Refuge and United Friendly is to be postponed for a second time due to the design of an option which will allow its own shareholders to receive a greater proportion of potential profits, known as orphan assets. Institutional shareholders had already forced Refuge to put the meeting off for 2 1/2 weeks as they felt they may lose the rights to Refuge's orphan assets. The meeting will be adjourned again from Thursday of next week until October 11.
THE TIMES
-- GOVERNOR SAYS CITY DOES NOT NEED EURO

The Governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, yesterday said that the City of London would still thrive whether or not Britain joins a single European currency. Speaking at the launch of the Bank's second quarterly report on technical preparations, Mr George said that it was difficult to identify any real risk for the City, and that the City is an international centre and not just a European one.
-- REED APPROACH FOR BLENHEIM

The Anglo-Dutch media group, Reed Elsevier has been identified as the bidder for the Blenheim Group at around 480p a share, valuing the group at 480 million pounds stg. It is thought that Blenheim, the exhibitions concern, want as much as 550p a share. News of the approach bid pushed Blenheim shares up 52.5p to 420p.
-- BSE CRISIS COSTS DALGETY OVER 15 MILLION POUNDS

The petfood giant, Dalgety, said yesterday that the BSE crisis had cost it more than 15 million pounds stg. The company that owns Spillers and Felix, said a steep rise in the cost of raw materials and the BSE crisis seriously affected four of their five businesses. Additionally UK petfoods performed below expectations due to lower sales volumes. The company made a pre-tax profit, excluding one-off items of 101.9 million pounds stg, 20 per cent down on last year.
THE GUARDIAN
-- MAGISTRATES SAY OLIVETTI CHIEF IS UNDER SUSPICION

Olivetti's managing director, Francesco Caio, has been formally placed under investigation by magistrates in Ivrea, on suspicion of publishing false company information. The move follows an interrogation of the company's former general manager, Renzo Francesconi, by the Ivrea investigators. Mr Francesconi resigned after alleging that Olivetti understated the company's real losses in the interim results issued on September 3.
-- TOP BOSSES TAKE 12.6 PER CENT RISE

According to research published today the annual rise in top company directors' pay has accelerated to 12.6 per cent this year. The report published by the employment consultancy Incomes Data Services, shows that basic salary plus benefits rose by an average of 7.1 per cent to 448,801 pounds stg, and annual bonus levels increased to an average 243,157 pounds stg.
-- 'OPEN SKIES' DARKEN OVER BA MERGER

Robert Crandall, the chairman of American Airlines, said yesterday that he would pull out of the proposed alliance with British Airways if talks between the US and Britain on a new 'open skies' agreement went on much longer. Mr Crandall, in Britain for a series of top level meetings with BA and ministers said that talks would have to be finalised before the end of the year.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- LEASE SNAG DELAYS SIGNET JEWELLERY SALE

Due to complex negotiations over property leases the sale of Signet's two jewellery businesses, H Samuel and Ernest Jones to Apax Partners, the venture capital group, has been delayed. Completion of the deal has been put on hold until a formula can be agreed to safeguard Signet from any future liability regarding the leases of more than 600 shops.
-- ECC LAUNCHES FRESH CUTS AFTER PROFITS COLLAPSE

The world's biggest producer of Kaolin, English China Clays yesterday reported pre-tax profits down from 55.3 million pounds stg to just 5.7 million pounds stg in the six months to June, and announced another round of restructuring with the intention of cutting 30 million pounds stg of costs in its kaolin business. Shares in the group fell 10p to 216.5p as brokers factored in a possible dividend cut to around 10.5p from last year's figure of 16.7p.
-- INDEPENDENT EYES NZ TAKEOVER

The Irish newspaper group, Independent Newspapers, yesterday made its largest ever takeover bid with a 460 million pounds stg offer for Wilson & Horton, New Zealand's largest newspaper company. Wilson & Horton runs New Zealand's most popular paper the Daily Herald with a circulation of 260,000 copies. Independent Newspapers gained effective control of 45 per cent of Wilson & Horton a year ago through a subsidiary company.
